subject.title: improve(setup): keep WSL operations inside the app-owned directory

question: Should standalone SetupEngine continue accepting existing safe custom WSL distro names, or should the project intentionally restrict all such names to the new ASCII 1–64-character grammar?
rationale: The path-safety objective is clear, but the PR changes an existing developer-facing configuration contract and can strand legacy cleanup or setup flows; source inspection and tests cannot choose that compatibility policy safely.

options.title: Preserve safe custom names
options.body: Keep canonical containment and reparse-point protections while allowing existing names that resolve to a safe immediate child of the app-owned WSL root.

options.title: Approve the narrower contract
options.body: Accept the ASCII-only restriction as an intentional breaking change and add explicit upgrade, cleanup, and compatibility coverage for prior custom names.

recommendation.title: Preserve safe custom names
recommendation.body: Keep canonical containment and reparse-point protections while allowing existing names that resolve to a safe immediate child of the app-owned WSL root.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the present policy and can clarify the intended SetupEngine compatibility boundary, although a project owner must make the final product decision.
